notes: Arabic source Arabic Tobit follows the Vulgate (Latin → Arabic) recension; English English follows Rahlfs Greek Septuagint. They are different recensions of the same book — narrative voice (3rd-person vs 1st-person), event ordering, and verse boundaries diverge.

This table covers OVERFLOW MAPPINGS — verses that exist in one translation past the other's end-of-chapter, plus a handful of well-attested mid-chapter shifts. Where both translations have a verse number with overlapping content (even if textually different), we let identity stand and the response shows the divergence honestly.

Mid-chapter Vulgate additions where en HAS the verse-number with different content are not flagged as `null` — adding null mappings there would silently strip out en's actual content. Instead, callers comparing ar-Vulgate-additions to en should consult this table directly.

All ar-only Vulgate insertions documented here as `null` are within the OVERFLOW range (ar v# > en chapter max), so the API correctly reports `present:false` with the `mapping_note` annotation rather than misaligning content.
